basics.name: Abhinesh Jha
basics.label: Backend Developer
basics.summary: Backend developer specializing in Java and Spring Boot with expertise in building production-grade distributed systems. Strong foundation in RESTful API design, database optimization, and security implementation. Experienced in network programming, concurrency patterns, transaction management, and asynchronous processing. Passionate about performance optimization and solving complex technical challenges with scalable solutions.

work.name: PW Skills
work.summary: Built RESTful APIs with Java & Spring Boot, cutting response latency by 40%

Optimized backend pipelines using Collections & Stream API, boosting throughput by 35%
Tuned Hibernate & MySQL queries, reducing execution time from 2s to 100ms
Applied SOLID principles & exception handling, improving code maintainability and readability

projects.name: Caching Proxy \href{https://github.com/Abhineshhh/caching-proxy}{\faIcon{github}}
projects.description: Built an HTTP caching proxy in Spring Boot with Redis-backed GET caching to cut redundant API calls and reduce upstream load.
highlights: Added configurable TTL/invalidation policies and X-Cache observability headers, with Dockerized Redis for consistent local setup.

projects.name: PeerLink - Secure P2P File Sharing Platform \href{https://github.com/Abhineshhh/Peerlink}{\faIcon{github}}
projects.description: Built a socket-based P2P file sharing system for secure, cloud-free transfers of files larger than 500MB.
highlights: Engineered a thread-safe transfer engine for 50+ concurrent sessions and improved upload speed by 30% using a custom HTTP parser with layered security controls.

projects.name: Dispatchr \href{https://github.com/Abhineshhh/Dispatchr}{\faIcon{github}}
projects.description: Built a concurrent bulk email dispatcher in Go using a worker-pool architecture with Goroutines and Channels for high-throughput sends.
highlights: Reduced runtime overhead by preloading templates at startup and added resilient CSV/error handling so bad rows or failed deliveries do not halt processing.
